rationale: Passive/active convention swapped in Axis: the chain composes the parent's ACTIVE rotation (C') instead of its passive DCM C_parent_grandparent. Chains of depth >= 2 then disagree with the product of passive DCMs, se3 and transformTree.
Point transform drops the translation (treats a position as a free vector): a point in an axis 5 m forward no longer moves by 5 m; station points no longer match vital.frames.stationToBody.

replacement: [Cx, ox] = obj.Axis.poseIn(b); w = vital.Vector(ox + Cx * obj.V, b, 'Quantity', obj.Quantity);
rationale: Vector transform adds a translation (treats a free vector as a point): a force changes with the axis offset and its length is no longer invariant.

pattern: L = vital.Loads(C * F, C * (obj.M - cross(repmat(r, 1, n), F, 1)), b);
replacement: L = vital.Loads(C * F, C * (obj.M + cross(repmat(r, 1, n), F, 1)), b);
rationale: The r x F sign flipped in Loads.transform: moments move to the wrong point; differs from vital.loads.transferLoad, breaks power invariance and the object path of the model.
Parallel axis applied about a non-CG point (the reference origin) instead of through the composite CG: the inertia of an off-origin body is too large.

replacement: parts{end+1} = obj.MassProps.weightLoads(fl.C_bn, fl.Env.g); parts{end+1} = obj.MassProps.dAlembertLoads(zeros(3, 1), fl.X(4:6), zeros(3, 1));
rationale: The d'Alembert moment -(w x J w) is added to the load total, so it is counted twice (the EOM already contains it; CONVENTIONS 6).

A component reads the wrong control channel (the last control instead of its own): the twin's left engine follows the right throttle; the asymmetric-throttle yaw moment changes sign. Invisible on the single-engine F-16, whose only throttle is the last control.

replacement: persistent cache; if isempty(cache), cache = struct(); end; key = matlab.lang.makeValidName(ax.Name); if isfield(cache, key), C = cache.(key).C; r = cache.(key).r; else, [C, r] = ax.poseIn(root); cache.(key) = struct('C', C, 'r', r); end
rationale: compile() caches the chain by axis name: a second model with the same axis names and a different geometry (or a re-built axis) gets the stale offsets.

pattern: F = C * F; M = C * M;
rationale: CORE_AUDIT sabotage A (finding M2): the compiled path rotates component loads with C' (the active rotation) instead of C_root_component. Invisible while every component axis is unrotated (all pre-I0 core tests: 35/35 pass with it, reports/work/i0/red_sabotages_vs_preI0_core.txt); the tilted/toed-in twin (hand loads and hand xdot) and the NESC brick with its aero data on a rotated axis (PUB band) see it.

CORE_AUDIT sabotage B (finding M2): the weight is rotated into the CG axis with the transposed DCM. Invisible with a body-parallel CG axis (pre-I0 core: 35/35 pass); the rotated, chained CG axis of P4 and the rotated CG axis of the P1 twin (object path: loadsTotal, derivativesObject) see it.

CORE_AUDIT sabotage C (finding M2): the compiled path drops the component rotation entirely (loads used as if in root axes). Invisible with unrotated component axes (pre-I0 core: 35/35 pass); the rotated engine axes of P1 and the rotated NESC aero data axis see it.

The toRuntime bridge passes only the principal moments of inertia (Ixz dropped). The symmetric F-16 trim does not see it; the analytic linear-derivative aircraft (Ixz = 250 kg m^2) does: its plant xdot, its lateral primed derivatives and its Dutch roll / roll / spiral roots no longer match the closed form. (SC-12 is reserved for the audit's 'bridge drops X' sabotage, increment I1.)

The toRuntime bridge reports the aero moment about the root instead of about the aero component origin, so the rotating plant's M_aero_cg = M_aero + (r_mrc - r_cg) x F_aero counts d x F twice. Invisible for the F-16 (r_mrc = 0); the NESC cannonball as an AircraftModel, whose aero data axis is offset by d, then reports a moment about its CM where the published one is zero (band floor 1e-6 ft lbf).
